Transformer Modeling I
Ideal voltage, current, and impedance relationships
Buxin She
Mike Wiegers Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

Lecture outline
1 Explain how AC excitation produces voltage transformation
2 Identify winding variables and apply four ideal assumptions
3 Derive voltage, current, power, and impedance relationships
A physical picture establishes the variables. The ideal assumptions then support one
relationship at a time.

Ideal-transformer summary
Ratio convention: define 𝑎 = 𝑁 𝐻 /𝑁𝐿 = 𝑉 𝐻 /𝑉𝐿 from fixed equipment-side
labels, independent of power-flow direction.
Current scaling: ideal current magnitude changes inversely with the turns ratio
while the declared polarity fixes phase.
Impedance referral: an impedance referred across the ideal transformer scales
by 𝑎2. Apply the referral once.
Power invariance: an ideal transformer preserves complex power, providing an
independent check on voltage and current scaling.
Freeze the H/L convention first. Every voltage, current, and impedance transformation
follows from it.
ECE 685 | Transformer Modeling I 38/38
